+title: Give the initial-leader LSP workers the shutdown flag of their tenure
+---
+## Problem
+`start_lsp_workers_if_leader` (`crates/swissarmyhammer-tools/src/mcp/server/code_context.rs`) reads `shared_db` and `leader_shutdown_flag()` from the workspace at the time the workers start. It does not use the flag of the tenure that started the supervisor. `spawn_drain_supervisor_and_health_loop` reads the tenure flag, then calls `start_workers`. If a step-down and a new promotion both occur between that read and the workspace lock, the LSP indexing workers of the old supervisor get the flag of the new tenure. Those workers then do not stop with the old tenure.
+
+The window is small (the re-election poll is 5 s). The promotion path (`start_indexing_workers_after_promotion`) already uses the tenure flag.
+
+## Fix
+- Give `start_lsp_workers_if_leader` the tenure flag from `spawn_lsp_health_loop`, and use it for `LspWorkerSetup::shutdown`.
+- Start no worker when that flag is set.
+
+## Tests
+- A unit test: a step-down and a promotion, then `start_lsp_workers_if_leader` with the old tenure flag starts no worker. #lsp-fix #bug
\ No newline at end of file

+  text: |-
+    Research done.
+    - `do_initialize_code_context` reads the tenure flag one time (`leader_shutdown`). After that, three places read `leader_shutdown_flag()` from the workspace again: `start_workers_if_leader`, `spawn_lsp_health_loop`, and `start_lsp_workers_if_leader`. The tenure flag is in scope at each of these places (from `do_initialize_code_context` or from `spawn_lsp_health_loop`). These are the places to fix.
+    - `handle_promotion_result` also reads `leader_shutdown_flag()`, but no tenure flag is in scope there: it is the first read after `try_promote`. No change there.
+    - Test seam: `LspSession::new(Arc::new(Mutex::new(None)), "rust")` gives a session with no LSP process. `spawn_lsp_workers_for_clients` binds the election request socket synchronously (`RequestServer::bind`), so the socket file at `socket_path()` is an observable sign that a worker started.
+    - Plan: `start_lsp_workers_if_leader` takes the tenure flag, checks it under the workspace lock (a step-down needs that lock, so the tenure cannot change during the read of `shared_db`), and returns before it starts a worker when the flag is set.
